items.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: Frank honed his craft with bands led by Lucky Millinder

ctx.x: Reedman Frank Wess is an important part of the Basie legacy. As half of the two tenor team in the reformed Basie band of the 50’s, he was instrumental in propelling the group to its highest popularity. Born in Kansas City in 1922, Frank honed his craft with bands led by Lucky Millinder, Eddie Haywood and Billy Eckstine. From 1953-64 he teamed with Frank Foster and Marshall Royal to solidify the great Basie sax section. Basie also employed Frank’s considerable arranging skills as well as his pioneering jazz work…

After the Basie years he found steady work in New York studios while keeping a presence on the jazz scene with the New York Jazz Quartet and Dameronia. In recent years, Frank has co-led a group with Frank Foster, performed briefly with Woody Herman and has become a featured player at jazz fests and parties across the country.
